ai.description: *Leptobrachium bompu* is a medium-sized toad (SVL 45–60 mm) with a dark grey-brown back and bright blue irises. It features a distinct, pale, glandular ridge behind the eye and lacks a visible tympanum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Leptobrachium bompu* is best distinguished by its unique, bright blue iris, which contrasts sharply with the dark, uniform coloration of other Indian *Leptobrachium* species.
ai.habitat: *Leptobrachium bompu* inhabits primary evergreen broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,700 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Eastern Spadefoot Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects on the forest floor while remaining hidden in leaf litter during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Leptobrachium bompu* breeds in streams during the monsoon (May–August). Females lay small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks or vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Leptobrachium bompu* is endemic to the Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary in Arunachal Pradesh, India, occurring in subtropical forests at elevations between 1,800 and 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: *Leptobrachium bompu* produces a series of short, metallic, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard emanating from rocky streams within dense, humid evergreen forests.
